source.title: Which Sparse Autoencoder Features Are Real? Model-X Knockoffs for False Discovery Rate Control

record.tranche_reason: Applies an SAE feature-selection analysis to Pythia-70M and reports results on features from that model; it does not reproduce the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature-selection and task-classification results on Pythia-70M, which bear on V4. Its discussion of superposition and polysemanticity is background, not a tested result. Knockoff parameters and the selection threshold are settings, not separate rows. It does not measure feature geometry, neuron polysemanticity, or causal feature effects.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pre-trained Pythia-70M SAE as a tool and reports how its own knockoff selection method performs: 129/512 latents selected at FDR 0.1. It does not test whether the model's features are superposed, or whether SAEs recover the model's features. Asking which SAE latents are statistically linked to SST-2 labels is a feature-validation question. It is not evidence for or against any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also frame the 129 selected latents as 'genuine'/'real' features. They describe the remaining 75% as noise or spurious correlations, which is a stronger framing than the record conveys. They still concede in the limitations that association does not imply causal importance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Gaussian Model-X knockoffs and knockoff+ on SAE activations for task-specific feature selection, rather than the original toy-network superposition experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: About 25% (129/512) of high-energy layer-3 SAE latents in Pythia-70M pass knockoff+ selection for SST-2 sentiment at q=0.1. Some latents have strongly negative knockoff statistics (as low as -0.445).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Only a minority of active SAE latents are statistically associated with a given downstream task once multiple testing is controlled.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one model, one layer, and one task, using 512 energy-selected features rather than the full SAE dictionary. The authors state that energy-based reduction may miss rare important features and that statistical association does not imply causal importance. The reported classifier result is training-set performance, and its feature set is described inconsistently in the body and figure caption. No control comparison is reported.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition or feature geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.

The study uses a pre-trained SAE but does not test whether features are distributed across neurons or whether the SAE recovers the model's features (no reconstruction, ground truth or neuron baseline).
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/tests/V4-supports judgment is overturned. The rows are outputs of the study's own method on a pre-trained SAE. They do not bear on whether SAEs recover superposed features. The energy filter keeps only the top 512 of 32,768 latents. The classifier accuracy is training-set only, and the body and figure caption describe its feature set inconsistently.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension sweep, sparsity transition, or feature geometry is tested.
No test of whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Tests task-associated features from one SAE, model, layer, and dataset; does not test how broadly features are distributed across neurons, generalization to other tasks or models, or causal feature recovery.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Applied Model-X knockoff+ selection to SAE features using logistic-regression feature importance.

conditions.value: 512 top features by average absolute activation energy, selected from 32,768

rows.measure: Number and proportion of candidate SAE features selected as task-associated by knockoff+
rows.note: The paper characterizes the selected features as carrying sentiment-related signal. This is task association under the study's procedure, not evidence of causal importance; the authors note that distinction.
rows.check: This is a selection value from the study's own method: knockoff+ count and threshold. It measures how many SAE latents are associated with sentiment labels. It does not measure whether the model holds sparse features that an SAE recovers, so it does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated an ℓ1-regularized logistic classifier using SAE features for SST-2 sentiment classification.
rows.note: The body describes the classifier as trained on the augmented design [X | X̃], while the Figure 1 caption says it uses only selected features; the text does not resolve this discrepancy. The result is training-set performance.
rows.check: This is the training-set accuracy of the study's own logistic classifier. The body says the classifier was fit on the augmented [X | X̃] design; the caption says selected features only. It reflects task decodability from SAE latents, not superposition or SAE recovery of model features. The 50% chance baseline is not a control for V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The analysis identifies task-associated SAE features, and the reported classifier accuracy exceeds random guessing (r1–r2).
